sections.content: You know *ya* with the *pretérito perfecto* from Unit 2: *Ya he preparado la cena*. Here you use it to answer an invitation: when you have already made plans or preparations, say so. *Ya* comes before *he* or *hemos*, and the participle follows.

items.spanish: Lo siento, ya he hecho un plan.
items.english: I'm sorry, I have already made a plan.
We have already accepted the invitation.

rows: Lo siento, ya he hecho un plan.
I'm sorry, I have already made a plan.

sections.content: *ya* can even stand alone as a one-word answer: to *¿Ya has cenado?*, a simple *Ya* means 'already done' — Spanish speakers use it as shorthand far more often than English uses a bare 'already'.
